title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme. G is a form of GL(2) (or SL(2)) given as the unit scheme G(M) (resp. the determinant-1 units SG(M)) of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M over S. The aim, continuing the 'loop equation' study, is to describe the scheme of solutions alpha of [alpha, rho] = xi for a given regular section rho, and then to decide when [alpha, beta] = rho is solvable.

(i) Regularity. rho is regular iff on every fibre the subalgebra generated by rho has rank 2, i.e. rho is nowhere fibrewise scalar. Then rho generates the quadratic algebra A_rho = O_S + O_S rho (10). A_rho is locally a direct summand of M as a module, so its formation commutes with base change.

(ii) Centralizers. One sets T_rho = units of A_rho (11) for G = G(M), i.e. the Weil restriction R_{A_rho/S} G_m. For G = SG(M) one takes the norm-1 units of A_rho (11 bis). These are the centralizers of rho, and the preceding corollary says the solution scheme of [alpha, rho] = xi is a right torsor under T_rho.

(iii) When T_rho is a torus. T_rho is a torus iff rho is fibrewise semisimple. Because rho is regular, this is equivalent to rho having two distinct eigenvalues in each fibre, i.e. the discriminant of its characteristic polynomial is invertible, i.e. A_rho is etale.

(iv) Example rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] in SL2(Z), the order-6 elliptic element with rho^3 = -1.
- Characteristic polynomial x^2 - x + 1, discriminant -3.
- A_rho is Z[zeta_6], the Eisenstein integers.
- T_rho is a torus away from 3. Over Spec Z it is not a torus in the strict sense: over F_3 one has A = F_3[x]/(x+1)^2, whose units are G_m x (unipotent).

(v) Next page. For sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 4) one gets A = Z[i], bad at 2.
- Torsors under the full unit group R_{A/S} G_m are Zariski-locally trivial (Hilbert 90 / Pic of semilocal rings).
- Torsors under the norm-1 subgroup need not be.
- Hence [alpha, beta] = rho is Zariski-locally solvable in G(M) but perhaps not in SG(M).
errors: No mathematical errors found. Computations check: rho^2 = [[-1,1],[-1,0]] and rho^3 = -I. The characteristic polynomial x^2 - x + 1 has discriminant -3, so rho is non-semisimple exactly in characteristic 3, consistent with the text.
Minor phrasing: 'qui est le cas en car. ≠ 3' refers to semisimplicity. The parenthetical gloss of 'tore' is partly illegible.

ideas.what: Centralizer of a regular element of a form of GL2/SL2 over a base equals the units (resp. norm-1 units) of the quadratic algebra O_S + O_S rho, locally a direct summand, so it commutes with base change
ideas.modern_name: centralizers of regular sections; Weil restriction R_{A/S} G_m and norm-one torus R^1_{A/S} G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA 3 (Demazure–Grothendieck), regular elements and centralizers; standard
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (Exp. XIII–XIV on regular elements, Cartan subgroups)

ideas.what: T_rho is a torus iff rho is fibrewise semisimple iff its two eigenvalues are distinct in each fibre (A_rho etale)
ideas.modern_name: etaleness of a quadratic algebra / discriminant criterion

ideas.what: The centralizer of the order-6 elliptic element of SL2(Z), viewed as a group scheme over Spec Z, is R_{Z[zeta_6]/Z} G_m. It degenerates at 3 into G_m times a unipotent group; for sigma (Z[i]) the degeneration is at 2
ideas.modern_name: Neron-type degeneration of tori at ramified primes; centralizers of elliptic elements as group schemes over Z

missed.claim: The page treats the centralizers of the elliptic generators of SL2(Z), relevant to the loop/Teichmüller-type equations, as integral group schemes with bad reduction at 2 and 3. This ties the 'loop equation' program to the arithmetic of Z[i] and Z[zeta_6]. It is a natural but routine observation and gives no new result on this page.
missed.quote: dans un sens strict T_ρ (en tant que schéma en groupes sur Spec Z) n'est pas un tore
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it illustrates why the primes 2 and 3 are special in the integral study of SL2(Z) relations, but this is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard SGA3-style algebra of centralizers of regular elements in rank-4 Azumaya algebras, applied to the two elliptic elements of SL2(Z). Correct and careful, but routine; no new result.

'loc. fact. direct' should read 'loc. facteur direct'.
The interlinear insertion after 'chaque fibre est' reads roughly '(et pas seulement en x ... solution)'; it is largely illegible.
